slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every number x, so that diamond of two x is equal to x plus five. And they're asking, what's diamond of fourteen?

slides: An operation is just a rule. You put a number in, and the rule tells you what comes out. Now look closely. The diamond works on two x, not on x, right? So what does this operation actually do? Is it adding five? No. It takes the number, divides it by two, and then adds five. Two x goes in, and x plus five comes out. Half of the number, plus five.

slides.say: So fourteen is not x. Fourteen is the two x. A lot of students put fourteen straight into x plus five. They get nineteen, and nineteen is waiting for them in the choices. That's the trap.
Two x is equal to fourteen. Divide by two, and x is equal to seven.
at: two x is equal to fourteen

slides.say: Now the rule says x plus five. [matter-of-fact] Seven plus five is twelve. And look, that's exactly half of fourteen, plus five, just like we said.
So number one is our answer.

slides: Whenever you see an operation like this, first ask what it really does to the number. Only then use the rule. [calmly] I'll see you in the next question.
